classification.difficultyReason: Substantial transfer, coordinated cases or justification beyond a direct worked-example substitution. The common denominator (x-1)(x+1) applies page 14's multi-fraction technique to both numerator terms and the outer denominator.

answer.worked:
Multiply the top and bottom by $x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)$.
$$\begin{align*}\dfrac{\dfrac1{x+1}+\dfrac1{x-1}}{1+\dfrac1{x^2-1}}&=\dfrac{(x-1)+(x+1)}{(x^2-1)+1}\\\dfrac{\dfrac1{x+1}+\dfrac1{x-1}}{1+\dfrac1{x^2-1}}&=\dfrac{2x}{x^2}\\\dfrac{\dfrac1{x+1}+\dfrac1{x-1}}{1+\dfrac1{x^2-1}}&=\dfrac2x.\end{align*}$$
Inner denominators require $x\ne-1,1$; the outer denominator also excludes $x=0$. Thus $x\ne-1,0,1$.
